entries.name: Christmas on the Julian calendar (January 7)
entries.capsule: Christmas as kept on January 7 by churches and families that still follow the older Julian church calendar.
entries.dateRule: December 25 on the Julian calendar, which is January 7 on the civil calendar from 1900 to 2099. Since 2023 the Orthodox Church of Ukraine, the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church and Ukraine's government have moved to December 25, so many Ukrainian families now keep Dec. 25; others keep Jan. 7. Ask the family.

dates.source: Fixed: Julian-calendar Christmas falls on Jan. 7 (Catholic Review/OSV News)

entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus, with Holy Supper (Sviat Vechir) on Christmas Eve.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: No opened Minnesota source describes a Jan. 7 celebration in 2026. St. Constantine Ukrainian Catholic Church in Minneapolis adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1943 and keeps Dec. 25. Which date each Minnesota Ukrainian Orthodox parish now uses could not be confirmed.

entries.name: Christmas (December 25)
entries.capsule: Christmas on December 25, now the official date in Ukraine and the date St. Constantine in Minneapolis has kept since 1943.
entries.dateRule: December 25 (Gregorian or Revised Julian calendar). Christmas Eve Holy Supper on Dec. 24.

dates.source: Fixed date; Ukraine moved official Christmas to Dec. 25 in 2023 (Catholic Review/OSV News)

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: St. Constantine Ukrainian Catholic Church adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1943, so its Christmas falls on Dec. 25. No opened 2026 Minnesota Christmas event listing was found.

entries.name: Easter (Western date)
entries.capsule: Easter on the Western date, kept by St. Constantine's Ukrainian Catholics, who use the Gregorian calendar; a season of pysanky and blessed baskets.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday after the first ecclesiastical full moon on or after March 21 (Gregorian). Ukrainian Catholic parishes on the Gregorian calendar use this date.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: St. Constantine holds a Palm Sunday dinner. The community center lists a Ukrainian Pysanka Festival and Easter Bazaar and pysanky classes, and its Lenten fish fry runs every Friday before Easter. St. Michael's and St. George's held its annual Palm Sunday Pysanka Festival on March 29, 2026.

entries.name: Orthodox Easter (Pascha)
entries.capsule: Easter on the Orthodox date, often a week or more after Western Easter, with blessing of Easter baskets.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday after the first full moon on or after the spring equinox, reckoned on the Julian calendar. Orthodox churches on the Revised Julian calendar still use this Easter date.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Minneapolis's St. Michael's and St. George's and Arden Hills' St. Katherine are Ukrainian Orthodox parishes. In 2026 Archbishop Daniel visited St. Katherine on the Fifth Sunday after Pascha (May 10, 2026), joined by St. Michael's parishioners. No opened source describes their 2026 Pascha services.

St. Michael's and St. George's promoted the 2026 fish fry starting Feb. 20, 2026, as supporting the community center and Cheremosh Dance Company.

entries.name: Vyshyvanka Day
entries.capsule: A day for wearing embroidered vyshyvanka shirts and blouses; Minnesotans have gathered at Boom Island Park.
entries.whatItMarks: Ukrainian embroidered dress and identity; MPR described the vyshyvanka as a form of spiritual armor in Ukrainian culture.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On Thursday, May 19, 2022, Ukrainian Minnesotans gathered at Boom Island Park in Minneapolis, where the Ukrainian Village Band played and people danced the arkan. No 2026 listing was found.

entries.name: Ivana Kupala (midsummer)
entries.capsule: Midsummer folk festival of wreaths, fire and song; the Ukrainian Village Band organizes a summertime Ivana Kupala ethno-festival.
entries.dateRule: Midsummer; the Minnesota event date is set by its organizer. No dated Minnesota listing was found.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The Cedar Cultural Center's 2025 listing says the Ukrainian Village Band organizes a summertime ethno-festival called Ivana Kupala; no date, place or year was given.

sources.title: Summer at The Cedar: Ukrainian Village Band

entries.name: Ukrainian Independence Day
entries.capsule: August 24 marks Ukraine's 1991 declaration of independence; Minnesotans gather at Boom Island Park in Minneapolis.
entries.whatItMarks: Ukraine's declaration of independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On Sunday, Aug. 24, 2025, the Ukrainian Community of Minnesota held a gathering at Boom Island Park with music, food and traditional dress. For the 30th anniversary in 2021, the governor proclaimed Aug. 24 Ukrainian Independence Commemoration Day, Hennepin County lit the Lowry Avenue Bridge in blue and yellow, and the community unfurled a 280-foot flag. No 2026 event report was found.

entries.name: Ukrainian Festival of Minnesota
entries.capsule: Free two-day festival of Ukrainian food, dance and music at the Ukrainian American Community Center; postponed in 2026, planned for Sept. 17-18, 2027.
entries.dateRule: Normally the third weekend of September, announced each year by the festival organizers.

dates.source: Postponed in 2026 during the community center's renovation (Ukrainian Festival MN)

entries.whatItMarks: A celebration and sharing of Ukrainian culture; donations support humanitarian aid for Ukraine.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Held at the Ukrainian American Community Center, 301 Main St. NE, Minneapolis, since 2006, with a Friday evening dance party and a Saturday of food, craft vendors, beer garden, Cheremosh dancers, a varenyky-eating contest and children's activities (2025 schedule: Sept. 19-20). Admission free.

minnesotaEvents.place: Ukrainian American Community Center, 301 Main St. NE, Minneapolis

entries.name: Holodomor Remembrance
entries.capsule: Remembers the millions who died in the 1932-33 man-made famine in Soviet Ukraine; Minnesota marks the last week of November.
entries.dateRule: Commonly the fourth Saturday of November. A 2023 Minnesota House resolution named the last week of November Holodomor Memorial Week; community pages give the Minnesota memorial day as Nov. 25 or Nov. 28.
entries.whatItMarks: The Holodomor (death by hunger), the 1932-33 famine engineered by Stalin's government.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: A 2018 commemoration at the community center honored survivors; on Nov. 30, 2022, the community marked the 90th anniversary with a service led by local priests, choirs and a Holodomor Museum exhibit; on Nov. 8, 2023, an event at the State Capitol Rotunda drew the First Lady of Minnesota, and a House resolution was introduced. No 2026 event listing was found.

minnesotaEvents.name: 90th anniversary Holodomor commemoration
minnesotaEvents.place: Minnesota State Capitol Rotunda, St. Paul

entries.name: Anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion
entries.capsule: February 24 marks the 2022 full-scale invasion; Minnesota's Ukrainian community holds commemorations, not celebrations.
entries.whatItMarks: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, and those lost since.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On Feb. 24, 2022, a rally was held outside St. Constantine. The governor proclaimed Feb. 24, 2024, Solidarity with Ukraine Day, presented at a State Capitol event. In February 2025 the community center held a packed commemoration attended by a U.S. senator from Minnesota and the mayor of Minneapolis. No 2026 report was found.
